messages:
maria gomez: Quick heads-up — I finished the Pharos-11b bring-up smoke. Ran FP16 baseline, INT8 via AQT, and INT6 aggressive quant. Putting the raw numbers here for quick triage.

josh wang: Awesome — can you paste the latency + per-token cost summary?

maria gomez: Sure. TL;DR: INT8 saves ~34% per-token compute cost vs FP16, INT6 saves ~53% but has a quality hit on long-form summaries. Latency median: FP16 65ms/token, INT8 72ms/token, INT6 70ms/token (weird). Tail (95p): FP16 120ms, INT8 160ms, INT6 270ms.

anika rao: Why is INT6 median slightly better than INT8?

maria gomez: I suspect batching differences + kernel path for INT6 has a faster fused path for short seqs; but KV cache behavior kills the tail on INT6. Need more microbench.

samir patel: What about quality? any automatic metrics + manual spot checks?

maria gomez: Auto: Rouge-L for summarization dropped: FP16 0.47 -> INT8 0.45 (-4%), INT6 0.40 (-15%). Instruction-following eval (our small 200-slice GTN set): pass@thresholds: FP16 92%, INT8 88%, INT6 77%.

josh wang: That's a pretty big drop at INT6. Product will care if summaries start hallucinating. Any sample diffs?

maria gomez: Pasted a couple inline examples below (short). Example A: FP16 correct entity resolution, INT6 sometimes hallucinates an extra date. Example B: INT6 truncates or repeats on long context.

anika rao: For routing decision, we should consider hybrid: INT8 for baseline, fallback to FP16 for flagged slices (long context / high-risk prompts). Use INT6 only for low-risk bulk generation?

samir patel: Agree. Also consider soft-fail: route first attempt to INT8 + cheap online quality check (heuristic) and if check fails, re-try FP16. That avoids tail latency explosions hitting users.

maria gomez: I ran a quick simulated cost model for our demo traffic (50M tokens/day). Numbers: FP16 cost = $X/day (baseline 100%), INT8 = ~66% of FP16, INT6 = ~47% of FP16. With hybrid routing (80% INT8, 20% FP16 for falls) we get ~74% cost of FP16 with quality on-par with product constraints.

josh wang: Can you add the per-call latency impact for the soft-retry strategy? Need to know SLO implications.

maria gomez: Soft-retry modeled: adds +120ms p95 on the subset that fails check (we modeled 8% retry rate). Overall p95 increases from 160ms to 180ms for that route. If we restrict retries to non-interactive batch jobs, impact negligible.

anika rao: Proposal: roll INT8 to canary at 5% traffic, run GTN trigger set + priming-heavy slices, monitor: hallucination rate on our heuristics, re-rank divergence, 95p latency. Gate: if hallucinations delta > 5% or median QoL drop > 3 points, pause.

samir patel: Ops notes: need to add a KV cache TTL tweak for INT6 path if we ever enable it; we've seen noisy KV invalidation causing tail. Also add a kernel fallback flag to avoid using the aggressive INT6 path for multi-turn chat until we understand it.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: pharos-11b-int8-canary -> starts 1780003600, traffic 5%. Notified #eng-ml and #eng-sre.

maria gomez: Next actions: (1) Josh — approve canary schedule and SLO guardrails? (2) Anika — prepare GTN slice set and priming-heavy prompts for the canary. (3) Samir — add KV TTL experiment and kernel-fallback flag to runtime. I'm happy to own the quality logging and cost sim updates.

josh wang: Approve canary window. Put an automated rollback if hallucination heuristics cross the threshold. :thumbsup:

anika rao: I'll push the GTN slices and a lightweight scorer that runs on canary traces.

samir patel: I'll add the runtime flags and a perf microbench we can run in-situ.

maria gomez: Great. Final note — recommend we do NOT enable INT6 for high-value interactive endpoints until we have more manual review. INT8 looks like the sweet spot for now.

josh wang: Agreed. Shipping plan looks solid. Thanks all. :rocket:
